chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

On the Day of qiyāmah, a man will come to another man and smear him with blood while the people are in the reckoning. He will say, “O servant of Allah, what do I have to do with you?” He will reply, “You helped against me on such-and-such a day with a word, so I was killed.”

key_terms.الْحِسَابِ: the reckoning in which deeds are examined and judged
key_terms.بِالدَّمِ: with blood, symbolizing culpability for unlawful killing
key_terms.بِكَلِمَةٍ: with a single word, indicating even verbal participation can incur guilt
key_terms.فَقُتِلْتُ: so I was killed, expressing the consequence of that assistance
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when all people are brought for final judgment

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show accountability for assisting in killing on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith depicts a scene from the Day of Judgment in which even verbal assistance in a wrongful killing is exposed and held to account. It emphasizes the grave moral weight of complicity in bloodshed and the certainty of reckoning for the rights of others.
